title: Naturality of canonical open restriction tensor comparison
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and U any open. Let R be over-site restriction followed by the canonical over equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits] on sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For the sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], there exist isomorphisms e(F,G): R(F \otimes G) \cong R(F) \otimes R(G), simultaneously natural in both module arguments: for maps f:F \to Fprime and g:G \to Gprime, R(f \otimes g) followed by e(Fprime,Gprime) equals e(F,G) followed by R(f) \otimes R(g). No quasi-coherence, flatness or nonempty-open hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 17.16.4, functoriality; used in the locality step of Tag 08DX, proof of (1)

proof.text: Apply exists_restriction_tensor_comparison to U.ι for each pair of modules. Its inverse is characterized by local pure tensors. Both naturality composites send a local pure tensor s tensor t to f(s) tensor g(t), so they agree by the sectionwise tensor universal property and sheafification. Conjugating with the comparisons gives naturality of the forward maps.

Scheme.Modules.overFunctorEquiv U naturally identifies the canonical over-site composite with restriction along U.ι. Transport the tensor comparisons through its components and the common SheafOfModules carrier of Scheme.Modules. Its naturality transports both module-map squares to the stated square. The empty open has the zero module category and introduces no exception.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_openRestriction_tensor_natural (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens) :
    let R :=
      SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U ⋙
        Equivalence.functor
          (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
          (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
          (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U)
    ∃ e : ∀ (F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)),
      R.obj (F ⊗ G) ≅ R.obj F ⊗ R.obj G,
      ∀ (F F' G G' : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))
        (f : F ⟶ F') (g : G ⟶ G'),
        R.map (f ⊗ₘ g) ≫ (e F' G').hom =
          (e F G).hom ≫ (R.map f ⊗ₘ R.map g)
